records.text: Owens said NATO created the International Police Task Force as an arm of the United Nations civilian police force, and she alleged that the United Nations and DynCorp were charged with trafficking children, forcing prostitution, and covering it up.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And in this case, it was the International Police Task Force. That was an arm of the United Nations Civilian Police Force. ... They were created by NATO. ... Except they were exactly the ones who were charged with trafficking the children, covering it up, the United Nations, DynCorp, forcing them into prostitution.

verification.notes: United Nations records directly contradict the claim that NATO created the task force: Security Council Resolution 1035 established the UN International Police Task Force. Congressional and rights reports substantiate trafficking allegations against some DynCorp and international personnel, but not the blanket formulation that the United Nations as an institution was charged with the crimes.

sources.title: United Nations Security Council Resolution 1035
sources.relevance: Official record shows the UN Security Council established the International Police Task Force.

sources.title: Hopes Betrayed
sources.relevance: Documents trafficking allegations involving individual international and DynCorp personnel while distinguishing institutional claims.

records.text: Owens said Dave Rubin's book falsely stated that Ukraine was a member of NATO.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And even if you go back to Dave Rubin's book, which I read, Don't Burn This Book, I knew he had no idea about foreign policy because there's a chapter where he actually published, I think this was back in 2020 when he published his book, that Ukraine was a member of NATO.

verification.notes: A searchable copy of the 2020 book contains the sentence that Ukraine gave up nuclear weapons to become a NATO country. NATO currently and explicitly states that Ukraine is a partner, not a member. Owens characterization of the published passage as false is therefore confirmed.

sources.title: Dave Rubin, Do Not Burn This Book
sources.relevance: Contains the published passage stating that Ukraine became a NATO country.

sources.title: NATO support for Ukraine
sources.relevance: Official NATO source explicitly states that Ukraine is not a NATO member.

records.text: Owens said the 19th Special Forces Airborne routinely deploys to Romania to train in unconventional warfare with Romanian special operations forces and NATO allies.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Particularly, the U.S. Army's 19 Special Forces Airborne routinely deploy, of all places, to Romania to conduct unconventional warfare. They train with Romanian special operations force, working alongside NATO allies.

verification.notes: Official U.S. Special Operations Command Europe reporting confirms that elements of the 19th Special Forces Group trained in Romania during Trojan Footprint 2019 with Romanian and other allied special operations forces and conducted unconventional-warfare training. The available official record verifies the described activity but not the broader claim that the unit routinely deploys to Romania.

sources.title: Green Beret Citizen Soldiers Make Their Mark at Trojan Footprint
sources.relevance: Official SOCEUR reporting confirms 19th SFG training with Romanian and allied SOF in Romania in 2019, but does not establish routine deployment there.
